_about: Hand-curated starting statuses from news research on 2026-10-06. seed-cities.js applies these only to cities that do not already have a record, so later edits and AI updates are never overwritten. Names match the MnDOT boundary layer after normalization (St. = Saint).

cities.name: Crystal
cities.summary: Police chief ended the program. All 6 cameras were removed and returned on Sep 9 and data sharing ended. No replacement planned.

sources.title: Crystal becomes latest city to drop Flock cameras

cities.name: Columbia Heights
cities.summary: Council voted unanimously to cancel the contract. All 12 cameras were disconnected and removed.

sources.title: Columbia Heights votes to end Flock contract

cities.name: West St. Paul
cities.summary: City manager suspended the contract and all 10 cameras were removed. Bringing them back would require a council vote.

sources.title: West St. Paul suspends Flock contract

cities.name: St. Paul
cities.summary: Council passed a unanimous non-binding resolution to end Flock use in the city and county. The police department's 2 fixed cameras were removed. The Ramsey County Sheriff's roughly 37 cameras remain.

sources.title: St. Paul City Council on Flock cameras
St. Paul to remove Flock cameras

cities.name: Brooklyn Park
cities.summary: Cancelled its Flock contract (8 cameras) in December 2025 and switched to Axon plate readers: 4 installed, 2 more planned.

sources.title: Multiple Minnesota cities cancel Flock contracts

cities.name: Champlin
cities.summary: All cameras were pulled offline after vandalism. The city calls it temporary but has no reinstatement timeline.

sources.title: Vandals force Champlin to pull Flock cameras

cities.name: Dayton
cities.summary: Council suspended all license plate reader programs through 2027 because the contract is locked in. Flock reinstalled 2 cameras without authorization in October; they have since been removed.

sources.title: Flock cameras installed in Dayton without permission

cities.name: Fridley
cities.summary: Kept 6 cameras. Disabled immigration searches in January, limited sharing to Minnesota agencies in February, and blocked 287(g) agencies in July. It had been the largest outside access point, with about 390,000 outside searches a month.

sources.title: Flock camera debate at Fridley City Council

cities.name: St. Louis Park
cities.summary: Council voted to keep cameras with required reason codes, denial of immigration searches, and quarterly audits.

sources.title: Flock cameras will remain active in SLP, with limitations

cities.name: Shakopee
cities.summary: 7 cameras, 5 working. Outside agencies now need a warrant. Considering 7-day retention; no council vote yet.

cities.name: Woodbury
cities.summary: 18 cameras per state reports. Residents asked for a pause in August; staff restricted outside access and are exploring a third-party review.

sources.title: Residents urge privacy review of Flock cameras

cities.name: Edina
cities.summary: Active, with reported counts from 19 to 34 cameras. Repeated vandalism. The city says it does not share with outside agencies. No council action.

sources.title: Edina Flock cameras still functional after vandalism

cities.name: Richfield
cities.summary: 10 cameras active. Residents petitioned and testified on Aug 25; no vote scheduled. Contract renews May 2027.

sources.title: Richfield residents ask city to end Flock use

cities.name: Lakeville
cities.summary: Council approved 17 to 20 cameras on Dec 15, 2025. Residents are urging the council to rescind.

cities.name: Brooklyn Center
cities.summary: State reports list 11 active cameras, but one outlet reported the city cut ties. Needs confirmation.

cities.name: Maplewood
cities.summary: Approved a 2-year pilot on Jul 14, 2025. About 17 cameras reportedly installed but not yet activated as of September 2026.

cities.name: Burnsville
cities.summary: Council endorsed 20 Flock cameras at about $65,000 a year.

cities.name: Minneapolis
cities.summary: Police use about 30 plate readers from Insight LPR, not Flock, per an Aug 4 city statement. A 9-4 council resolution urges Hennepin County and the U of M to drop Flock.

cities.name: Eden Prairie
cities.summary: Uses Motorola plate readers, not Flock. No changes planned.

sources.title: Eden Prairie police address ALPR privacy concerns

cities.name: Plymouth
cities.summary: Council voted on Sep 22 to discontinue all 16 Flock cameras, with the mayor the sole dissent. As of October the cameras have not been removed or covered.

cities.name: Shorewood
cities.summary: South Lake Minnetonka Police are ending Flock on Dec 31, 2026. Shorewood's single camera is already out of service, covered with a garbage bag.

cities.name: Spring Park
cities.summary: Cancelled its Flock contract in September 2026.

cities.name: Excelsior
cities.summary: Policed by South Lake Minnetonka Police, which ends its Flock program on Dec 31, 2026.

cities.name: Greenwood
cities.summary: Policed by South Lake Minnetonka Police, which ends its Flock program on Dec 31, 2026.

cities.name: Tonka Bay
cities.summary: Policed by South Lake Minnetonka Police, which ends its Flock program on Dec 31, 2026.

cities.name: Mound
cities.summary: Policed by Orono Police. Mound never pursued Flock and no cameras were ever installed.

cities.name: Minnetonka Beach
cities.summary: The city has no plate reader cameras.

cities.name: Woodland
cities.summary: Has an active Flock contract.

trackerActive._about: Active Flock deployments with no reported cancellation, from the mnprivacy.org tracker (built from state-mandated BCA reports). Camera counts are reported counts.

sheriffContract._about: Cities with no police department of their own, mapped to the agency that polices them (a county sheriff or a contract police department). They inherit that agency's status until their own is known. Townships are added automatically.
